subject: Startups
title: Network Effects and Winner-Take-All
description: A micro-lesson that makes Network Effects and Winner-Take-All usable.

hook.text: Facebook wasn't the first social network. Myspace, Friendster, and Hi5 came first. But Facebook won everything.

buildup.text: Network effects mean a product gets more valuable as more people use it. Each new user benefits all existing users.

discovery.text: Once a network reaches critical mass, switching costs become enormous. Your friends are there, so you stay.

twist.text: This creates winner-take-all markets. The #1 player gets 80% of the value, #2 gets 15%, and others fights for scraps.

climax.text: Uber, Airbnb, and LinkedIn all leveraged network effects to become near-monopolies in their category.

punchline.text: In network-effect businesses, second place is last place.

quiz.question: What are network effects?
options: When a company builds multiple products
When a product gets more valuable as more people use it
When networks of computers process data faster
